answer: A trust-graph protocol defends an AI-agent economy from Sybil attacks by restricting entry into a verified peer garden. Nodes evaluate candidates via random-walk queries that must echo back across bilateral edges anchored to a cryptographic stake relic. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of establishing collateralized trust links with honest nodes per identity. However, topological bottlenecks can isolate sparse clusters, spuriously rejecting legitimate peripheral agents.
